claims.text: Adding titanium to an Al-Cr-Fe-Mn lightweight alloy will improve mechanical performance relative to the unmodified alloy.
Adding titanium to an Al-Cr-Fe-Mn lightweight alloy will improve corrosion resistance relative to the unmodified alloy.
Adding titanium to an Al-Cr-Fe-Mn lightweight alloy will improve high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the unmodified alloy.
The titanium-modified alloy will retain low density.
Al-Cr-Fe-Mn is a lightweight high-entropy-alloy baseline.
High-entropy alloys are generally composed of five or more elements in equimolar or near-equimolar ratios.
High mixing entropy stabilizes a disordered solid-solution state in high-entropy alloys.
The titanium-modified Al-Cr-Fe-Mn alloy will possess a disordered solid-solution structure.
The titanium-modified Al-Cr-Fe-Mn alloy will possess a homogeneous amorphous structure.
Titanium-induced changes in crystal structure and lattice distortion will improve mechanical properties.
Chemical disorder and a homogeneous amorphous structure will improve corrosion resistance.
High mixing entropy and titanium-induced lattice effects will improve high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The proposed alloy is intended for weight-sensitive aerospace and rail-transportation applications.
The titanium addition must not significantly increase alloy density.
The effects of titanium on crystal structure and lattice distortion in the proposed alloy are not well established.
Failure to obtain significant improvements in all three property categories while retaining low density would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline is called a high-entropy alloy but is specified only as Al-Cr-Fe-Mn, whereas the boundary requires five or more elements. Titanium addition would create five elements, but the unmodified baseline does not satisfy the stated definition.

The mediator simultaneously specifies a disordered solid solution and a homogeneous amorphous structure, while the mechanism invokes crystal structure and lattice distortion. A fully amorphous phase lacks the crystalline lattice required for conventional lattice-distortion and crystalline solid-solution descriptions.
